findings.evidence: Lines 122–125 and 137–140 contain `(prefixSplitEquiv r).symm ... n`; `rg -n 'prefixConcat|prefixSplitEquiv'` finds no `prefixConcat` declaration, while line 105 establishes the local `prefixSplitEquiv_symm_apply` naming precedent.
findings.fix: Rename both consistently with the adjacent `prefixSplitEquiv_symm_apply`, e.g. `prefixSplitEquiv_symm_apply_prefix_processShift` and `prefixSplitEquiv_symm_apply_prefix_processCons`.
findings.issue: `prefixConcat_processShift_apply` and `prefixConcat_processCons_apply` (line 137) name an undeclared `prefixConcat`, while both conclusions evaluate `(prefixSplitEquiv r).symm`; this violates the convention that theorem names describe the conclusion and `_apply` names the evaluated function.

summary: Two helper names refer to a nonexistent `prefixConcat` operation instead of the equivalence actually evaluated in their conclusions.
